- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to reflect risk-off or market correction bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use 3-period moving average to smooth.
- If 3–5 consecutive forecast days are below true outcome, model exhibits mean reversion bias; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day to catch rebound.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term sentiment-driven reversals; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days to anchor forecast mid-point.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33 within 3 days), model lags in adjusting; apply 1–2 day lag correction to forecast decline or rise.
